title: connectors: auto-shelf readiness — declarative `include` and a loud Swagger 2.0 refusal for connector-openapi; `tools/list` pagination, fatal 401 and a tool-snapshot hash for connector-mcp; an offline spec-normalization tool
body:
**Filing gate ③** (maintainer-directed task). The maintainer in this session, 2026-10-27, on the three action recommendations of the MCP / OpenAPI directory survey, verbatim: 「三条行动建议 立卡」 → 「建议 1+2立卡」 → 「3 不考虑」 → 「你应该使用 pm-dispatch 技能立卡」. This card is recommendation 1. Recommendation 2 is the sibling card filed in the same batch; recommendation 3 (China-market seed lists) is not filed, per 「3 不考虑」.

**Filed by** `session_01J8VVAjRKqdoEYQ4hXxtBuf`. ⛔ Not a claim. Lane suggestion: `domain:server` (`packages/connectors/*`; the normalization tool's home is triage's call, candidates below). Triage sets labels and priority.

**Business reason.** The marketplace plans an "auto-shelf": external MCP servers and OpenAPI documents turned into installable declarative connector Apps with no hand-written code. A survey run on 2026-10-27 (cloud session `session_01J8VVAkBLWGU85ggFfUbRV3`; its report lives only in that session's worktree, the figures below are reproduced with their upstream sources) found that today only a small slice of either catalogue can be instantiated with the existing providers, and that two of the blockers fail **silently**:

- Official MCP Registry, full crawl of `GET /v0/servers` on 2026-10-27: 50,913 servers (latest versions); 66% carry a remote endpoint, 97% of those Streamable HTTP; 5,695 declare a static secret header. Entries whose tool list exceeds one `tools/list` page lose every tool past the first page today, and a server that answers 401 is retried as "upstream unavailable" instead of failing loudly as a configuration fault.
- APIs.guru `list.json` (gh-pages snapshot read 2026-10-27): 2,529 APIs, **39.9% Swagger 2.0**. A 2.0 document loads today without any version check: `host`/`basePath` are ignored and `body`/`formData` parameters are dropped, so the instance comes up with wrong actions and no error. Large 3.x documents (GitHub REST 1,242 operations, Microsoft Graph about 17.9k) expose every operation because the declarative `openapi` provider has no operation allowlist.

**Who acts.** The `domain:server` seat, one PR per slice below (slices 1–3 are independent; slice 4 may land anywhere triage places it). Reader of the result: the marketplace shelf pipeline (cloud repository) consumes the normalized documents and the `include` lists; app authors read the new `providerConfig.include` key from `content/docs/automation/connectors`.

**Dedupe** (semantic issue search, `objectstack-ai/objectstack`, open and closed, 2026-10-27): "connector-openapi declarative include operation whitelist reject Swagger 2.0 dereference $ref YAML spec normalization" → 2 hits, neither this (#5168 closed: `$ref` dangling in the platform's own published OpenAPI document; #4579 closed: `openApi31` declared-not-enforced). "connector-mcp tools/list pagination cursor 401 unauthorized retry fatal tool snapshot hash drift rug-pull" → 8 hits, none on the outbound client (#20791 and the rest are the inbound MCP server surface; #8034 is the inbound stdio transport). #26702 (open, outbound OAuth) is adjacent, not overlapping: this card adds nothing to the auth model.

### Governing text

- **ADR-0097 §2 / §5** (`docs/adr/0097-declarative-connector-instances.md`): a declarative instance is `provider` + `providerConfig` validated by the provider; "Nothing else is authored on the instance". Re-check: `git grep -n "providerConfig" origin/main -- docs/adr/0097-declarative-connector-instances.md`.
- **ADR-0024** (`docs/adr/0024-mcp-connectors.md`): MCP tools become connector actions after one `tools/list`; stdio is default-deny. Re-check: `git grep -n "tools/list" origin/main -- docs/adr/0024-mcp-connectors.md`.
- **ADR-0023** (`docs/adr/0023-openapi-to-connector-generator.md`): the generator consumes an OpenAPI 3.x document; "The caller is responsible for loading and de-referencing ($ref) the doc" (`packages/connectors/connector-openapi/src/openapi-connector.ts:45-46`). Re-check: `git grep -n "de-referencing" origin/main -- packages/connectors/connector-openapi/src`.
- **AGENTS.md Prime Directive #12** (contract-first; "reject it at authoring/publish … so the error surfaces loudly — ⛔ never add a lenient alias or `??` fallback in a consumer"). A Swagger 2.0 document silently mis-mapped is exactly the lenient consumer this directive forbids.
- **AGENTS.md Prime Directive #10** (never advertise a capability the runtime does not deliver): a provider that "loads" 2.0 but drops its parameters advertises support it does not have.

**Protocol statement.** `Metadata-protocol: added` for slice 1 only — a new `include` key on the `openapi` provider's `providerConfig` (provider-validated, no `packages/spec` schema change; the MCP provider already carries the same key, `packages/connectors/connector-mcp/src/mcp-provider.ts:198-201`). Slices 2–4 change runtime behaviour and tooling, not the authoring surface. `Skills-docs: follow-up owed — content/docs/automation/connectors` for the `include` key.

### Premises (each with a re-check; read at `c3fb185a`)

1. The declarative `openapi` provider accepts only `spec` and `baseUrl`; the `include` predicate exists only on the programmatic `createOpenApiConnector` config. Re-check: `git grep -n "include" origin/main -- packages/connectors/connector-openapi/src/openapi-provider.ts` (expected 0 hits) and `git grep -n "include?: (op: OperationInfo)" origin/main -- packages/connectors/connector-openapi/src/openapi-connector.ts`.
2. No OpenAPI version check exists in the provider or generator. Re-check: `git grep -n -i "swagger" origin/main -- packages/connectors/connector-openapi/src` (expected 0 hits).
3. A URL `spec` is fetched again on every materialization with no integrity hash. Re-check: `git grep -n "loadOpenApiDocument" origin/main -- packages/connectors/connector-openapi/src/openapi-provider.ts`.
4. `connector-mcp` calls `listTools()` once with no cursor loop. Re-check: `git grep -n "listTools\|nextCursor" origin/main -- packages/connectors/connector-mcp/src/mcp-connector.ts` (expected: `listTools` hits, no `nextCursor`).
5. Every post-transport error, a rejected credential included, is wrapped as `ConnectorUpstreamUnavailableError` and retried. Re-check: `git grep -n "A credential the" origin/main -- packages/connectors/connector-mcp/src/mcp-provider.ts`.

### Work

1. **`connector-openapi`: declarative `include`.** `providerConfig.include: string[]` of `operationId`s (or the generated `method_path` key when `operationId` is absent), mapped onto the existing `include` predicate. An entry naming an operation the document does not carry is a fatal configuration fault at materialization (loud), not ignored.
2. **`connector-openapi`: refuse Swagger 2.0 at load.** `loadOpenApiDocument` checks the `openapi` field: absent or not `3.x` (a `swagger: "2.0"` document included) is a fatal configuration fault naming the file and the remedy ("convert to OpenAPI 3.x offline; see the normalization tool"). No conversion inside the runtime.
3. **`connector-mcp`: three hardenings.** (a) `tools/list` follows `nextCursor` until exhausted, with a bounded page count; (b) a 401 / 403 from the server during connect, handshake or `tools/list` is a fatal configuration fault, not `ConnectorUpstreamUnavailableError` (the comment at `mcp-provider.ts:213-221` records today's opposite choice and why; this card reverses it on the survey's reading that OAuth-protected vendor servers are the common case, and a retried 401 is noise that hides a misconfiguration); (c) `providerConfig.toolsSnapshotSha256` (optional): when set, the hash of the selected tools' `name` + `description` + `inputSchema` (canonical JSON) is compared on every materialization; a mismatch marks the instance `degraded` with a message naming the changed tool, so a server-side rewrite of a tool's description or schema (the "rug-pull" class) is visible instead of silently accepted. `include` already keeps newly added tools out; this closes the remaining gap.
4. **Offline spec-normalization tool** (home per triage: a `packages/cli` subcommand, or a script under `packages/connectors/connector-openapi/`): input an OpenAPI/Swagger URL or file; output a normalized 3.x JSON document (YAML→JSON, 2.0→3.0 conversion, bundle + dereference of `$ref`, `servers[0].url` made absolute), its sha256, and a generated `include` list from an allow-pattern. The shelf pipeline and app authors run it; the runtime never converts.

### Acceptance

- A declarative `openapi` instance with `include: ['listCustomers']` against a 3.x document exposes exactly that action; `include: ['nope']` refuses at materialization with the operation name in the message.
- A `swagger: "2.0"` document is refused at load with a message naming the file and the offline conversion; the instance never comes up half-mapped.
- Against a test MCP server that pages `tools/list` in two pages, every tool is discovered; against one that answers 401, the instance is a fatal configuration fault with no retry loop; with `toolsSnapshotSha256` set and one tool description changed server-side, the instance is `degraded` naming that tool.
- The normalization tool turns the Stripe (`stripe/openapi`, 3.0.0, MIT) and DocuSign (`docusign/OpenAPI-Specifications`, Swagger 2.0, MIT) documents into 3.x JSON that the provider loads without dangling `$ref`s; a changeset for each touched package.

### Out of scope

- The auth model (OAuth2, app-credential exchange, request signing): #26702 and the sibling card.
- The shelf itself (ingestion from the MCP Registry, listing generation, the first 20–30 seeds): cloud-repository work that consumes this card's outputs.
- Legacy SSE transport (about 2% of remote endpoints in the crawl): deliberately not done.
- form-urlencoded / multipart request bodies (Stripe write operations): a separate card if a consumer appears.

### Related

#26702 (outbound OAuth, open) · ADR-0097 · ADR-0023 · ADR-0024 · ADR-0022 · #26582 (Company Core decision, unrelated lane, same survey batch).
